ctx.x: The Prophets. By the way, talking about The Prophets. On a concert that I directed at Xavier University, it was in the month of December, I think, of 1932. I had a group, an orchestra. And speaking about this opera, The Prophets, we played The March for The Prophets. As the first number on that program. I'll never forget that. Was that by Meyerbeer?
By Meyerbeer. I think I have the program of that opera, at the French Opera. And...let's see...

I'm sorry I didn't get it out. But I have the program of that concert... Someday, maybe we can come back sometime and look over those. I have the program of that concert. Well, I directed that program. That's it. And it was quite a success. Now, myself, I had to make some substitute on that occasion. We didn't have any French horns. We didn't have no bassoons. We didn't have no oboe. But this is what I did. We had an orchestra of 26 pieces. I used a C clarinet, besides the first and second B flat. Yes. Yes. I…
